test.summary: SPM – OKR – Child OKRs inherit restrictions from parent OKR
test.description:
This test verifies inheriting restrictions from a parent OKR to its child OKRs.

*Validation scope:*

* Applying restrictions to a parent OKR
* Verifying restrictions are automatically inherited by all existing child OKRs
* Verifying restrictions are inherited by newly created child OKRs
* Verifying restrictions are propagated through all hierarchy levels (children and descendants)
* Verifying inherited restrictions cannot be manually modified on child OKRs
* Verifying changes to parent restrictions are reflected in all child OKRs

*Validation scope:*

* Applying restrictions to a parent OKR

* Verifying restrictions are inherited by newly created child OKRs
* Verifying restrictions are propagated through all hierarchy levels (children and descendants)
* Verifying inherited restrictions cannot be manually modified on child OKRs
* Verifying changes to parent restrictions are reflected in all child OKRs

1. *Preconditions:*

* Strategic Theme, Objective and Key Result are created
* Box scope is defined by Strategic theme and OKR task structure is enabled in this box
* Admin user and regular user (user B) are prepared

2. As admin user Open OKR Overview of boxName

* Strategic Theme 1

4. As admin user Open Strategic theme 1 → Click in Restriction button in the upper right corner → Open dropdown and set "*Only specific people or teams can view or edit*". Click Save

5. Click back to Overview →  Open Objective 1 and hover over to Restriction button
   Expected: The restriction is enabled and the *Restrictions button* is displayed in red color. Tooltip with message" *Restricted by the parent "Parent-Key" - Only specific people or teams can view or edit*.
6. Click back to Overview → Open Key result 1 and hover over to Restriction button
   Expected: The restriction is enabled and the *Restrictions button* is displayed in red color. Tooltip with message" *Restricted by the parent "Parent-Key" - Only specific people or teams can view or edit*.
7. Click Restriction button
   Expected: The *View restrictions* modal is displayed. The parent OKR key (*ST*) is visible, indicating that restrictions are inherited from the parent. Restriction settings is disabled and cannot be edited in this view.
